claims.statement: For the repository full-line kernel K(t)=Phi(|t|)/2, the Dimitrov-Xu order-two correlation satisfies nu_2(2u)=4 C(u), where C(u)=integral r^2 K(u+r)K(u-r) dr, and the tilted kernel satisfies Psi_y(2u)=4 cosh(2yu) C(u).
Using the Dimitrov-Xu theorem and Wiener's L1 Tauberian theorem, RH is equivalent to strict positivity of the Fourier transform of D_y(u)=cosh(2yu)C(u) for every real frequency and every 0<|y|<1/2.

If H_y(q)=D_y(sqrt(q)) is completely monotone on q>=0 for every 0<|y|<1/2, then D_y is a positive Gaussian mixture with strictly positive Fourier transform, hence RH follows. Complete monotonicity in all orders is not proved.
The internal-tilt kernel J_y(u)=integral r^2 cosh(2yr)K(u+r)K(u-r)dr satisfies 4 Fourier[J_y](2x)=|f'(x+iy)|^2-Re(f''(x+iy) conjugate(f(x+iy))) for f(z)=integral K(t)exp(-izt)dt.
The external Dimitrov-Xu tilt D_y and the internal Jensen tilt J_y are distinct for general y!=0 and coincide only at y=0.

The existing SOH-G004 channel curvature and variance bounds imply (log Phi)''<-10. Consequently for C(u)=integral r^2 K(u+r)K(u-r)dr one has -C'(u)/C(u)>20u for u>0. Hence for H_y(q)=cosh(2y sqrt(q))C(sqrt(q)), every 0<|y|<1/2 satisfies -H_y'(q)/H_y(q)>10-|y|tanh(2|y|sqrt(q))/sqrt(q)>19/2, with the q=0 value obtained by continuity. Therefore H_y'(q)<0 globally.
Integrating the SOH-G024-F logarithmic-slope bound gives H_y(q)<H_y(0)exp(-19q/2) for q>0, equivalently D_y(u)<D_y(0)exp(-19u^2/2) for u!=0, uniformly for every 0<|y|<1/2.

For f(z)=Fourier[K](z), Fourier[nu_2](z)=2(f'(z)^2-f(z)f''(z)), and the external tilted family satisfies 4 Fourier[D_y](2x)=Re(f'(x+iy)^2-f(x+iy)f''(x+iy)). This is distinct from the internal J_y conjugate-modulus identity.

With S_y(q)=-d/dq log H_y(q), one has H_y''/H_y=S_y^2-S_y'. Therefore the second complete-monotonicity inequality is exactly equivalent to S_y'<=S_y^2. SOH-G024 proves S_y>19/2 but does not prove the Riccati inequality globally.

Under the normalized bridge measure dmu_u proportional to r^2 K(u+r)K(u-r)dr/C(u), with A=L'(u+r)+L'(u-r), B=L''(u+r)+L''(u-r), R=-C'/C=E[A], and R'=E[B]-Var(A), define a=|y|, T=2a tanh(2au), N=R-T. Then 4u^3 H_y''(u^2)/H_y(u^2)=N+u[N^2+Var(A)-E[B]+4a^2 sech^2(2au)]. Its global non-negativity is the second-order complete-monotonicity obligation.

For D_u(r)=L'(u+r)-L'(u-r), the normalized bridge measure satisfies E[r^(2n+1) D_u(r)]=(2n+3)E[r^(2n)] for every n>=0. The G004 bound L''>10 implies E[r^(2n+2)]<(2n+3)E[r^(2n)]/20 and therefore E[r^(2n)]<(2n+1)!!/20^n. Consequently E[exp(lambda r^2)]<=(1-lambda/10)^(-3/2) for 0<=lambda<10.

The G004 theta-channel estimates also imply the companion curvature envelope 10<L''(s)<21 exp(2|s|). Combining this with the bridge exponential-moment hierarchy gives E[B_u]<36 e exp(2u). A sharpened lower bound gives N_y(u)>6 exp(2u) for u>=1/2. Hence N_y(u)^2>E[B_u], and the exact bridge normal form proves H_y''(q)>0 for every q>=1/4 and every 0<|y|<1/2. The compact core 0<=q<1/4 remains open.

Finite five-point diagnostics through derivative order four on the declared Riemann-kernel grid are recorded only as FINITE_DIAGNOSTIC_NOT_PROOF for derivative orders two through four; first-order monotonicity is independently proved analytically and second-order monotonicity is analytically proved only for q>=1/4.

open_obligations: prove H_y''(q)>=0 on the remaining compact core 0<=q<1/4 for every 0<|y|<1/2
equivalently close the second-order bridge/Riccati inequality on that compact core
prove complete monotonicity of H_y for derivative orders m>=3
cover every q>=0 and every 0<|y|<1/2 for all higher orders
or independently prove strict positivity of Re(f'^2-f f'') on the full external strip
SOH-C005 full admissible Weil positivity remains open
